result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_node_ids_by_edge_id()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get edge (source, target) node IDs by edge ID. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L6735-L6805){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_node_ids_by_edge_id(edge_id) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Node ids by edge id](/assets/graphs/get-node-ids-by-edge-id.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared four-node graph with node ids in pills and edge ids on the edges. The queried edge 3, between B and C, is in the accent color, and so are its endpoints B and C with ids 2 and 3. The card returns the (source, target) pair (2, 3)." width="100%"} Retrieves the source and target node IDs for a specific edge using its edge ID. Returns `None` if the edge ID doesn't exist. This is a lightweight alternative to `get_edge()` when only the endpoints matter, for example when walking over edge IDs from `get_edge_ids()` or `get_selected_edge_ids()` and needing to know which nodes each edge joins. In a directed graph the pair gives the edge's direction; in an undirected graph it simply records the order in which the endpoints were given to `add_edge()`. The result contains node IDs, so use `get_label_from_id()` to turn them into labels. The lookup scans the edge list, so for retrieving the endpoints of every edge, `get_edges_as_tuples()` is faster than calling this method once per edge. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edge_id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The integer ID of the edge to look up, as returned by `get_edge_ids()`, `find_edge_ids()`, and similar methods. An ID that doesn't exist (including the ID of a deleted edge) returns `None`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[int, int] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A tuple of (`source_node_id`, `target_node_id`) if the edge exists, `None` otherwise. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Given an edge ID, this returns the `(source, target)` node IDs it connects: ::: {#9c5c33c4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") ) edge_id = graph.get_edge_ids()[0] graph.get_node_ids_by_edge_id(edge_id=edge_id) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (1, 2) ``` ::: ::: Looking up a nonexistent edge ID returns `None` rather than raising: ::: {#a4e3dc77 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_node_ids_by_edge_id(edge_id=9999) ``` ::: In a directed graph the pair follows the edge's direction. Translating the IDs to labels shows that edge `2` runs from `"Carol"` to `"Alice"`: ::: {#0a14a3c3 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} directed = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["Alice", "Bob", "Carol"]) .add_edges([("Alice", "Bob"), ("Carol", "Alice")]) ) source, target = directed.get_node_ids_by_edge_id(2) directed.get_label_from_id(source), directed.get_label_from_id(target) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ('Carol', 'Alice') ``` ::: :::
